Little Savage Mountain rises to 2,818 feet in Pennsylvania. The Little Savage Mountain Trail covers 2.1 miles round trip (out-and-back) with about 154 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 39.7676, -78.90974 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 75 miles southeast of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Spring through fall is the main season. Conditions change fast in the shoulder months — check a point forecast for the summit, not the nearest town, before you commit.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 1.0 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go.
